title: mason connector protocol, major 1
description: The normative wire contract between mason and an external connector. One connector-initiated WebSocket carries JSON-RPC 2.0 in both directions; MCP over Streamable HTTP stays the tools transport and is not described here. Every message below is the params or result of one JSON-RPC method. A field a receiver does not know is ignored; a field this document requires and does not receive is a protocol error.

version.description: The protocol version a side speaks. Mason negotiated one major per socket; a connector that speaks only other majors is refused at the handshake.

minors.description: Optional minors the sender implements, highest last. Mason answers with the highest one both sides know, so an addition within a major never fails a handshake.

capability.description: A content or delivery capability, negotiated independently of any privilege grant. An origin is only ever sent what it claims.

stateScope.description: A slice of mason's state a connector may mirror. Reasoning, tool arguments, tool output and the raw conversation are in none of them.

face.description: One of the three things a connector can be. They are faces of one connector, never types of connector.

externalActor.description: A person as the connector's medium names them. Mason maps it to a roster name and decides what it may do; a display name never grants owner identity or approval authority.

externalConversation.description: A place as the medium names it. `kind` decides whether a reply is private: `room` is a space that speaks to more than one person.

origin.description: Where an inbound item came from, and therefore where its reply goes. Mason routes a reply here; it never names a vendor's tool.

blocks.description: Message content as typed blocks. A file is a content id that crosses through the transfer endpoints, never a path or a base64 blob.

submissionMode.description: What to do with a submission that arrives while a turn is running. Absent means the operator-configured default.

accepted.description: The durable claim of an inbound item. A duplicate id is answered with the same claim, `duplicate: true`, and no second logical operation.

helloRequest.description: `mason/hello` params: the first call on every socket. It declares what the connector is and what it can render; the operator's configuration decides what it may do.

faces.description: The faces this connector implements. Declaring one is a request, not a grant.

url.description: Where mason opens its directional MCP connection. Mason uses its own credential here; this field is an address, not a secret.

kinds.description: The structured `kind` strings this connector may fire. The operator maps them to hooks; mason never invents a vendor-specific one.

helloResult.description: The negotiation. Only granted faces appear in `faces`; a face the connector implements but the operator did not grant is named in `inactive` with a reason instead of failing the socket.

connector.description: The connector name mason configured under. It may differ from the name advertised.

actors.description: The external actors mason maps to a roster name. An actor absent from this list is refused unless the entry permits unattributed participants.

conversations.description: The rooms and conversations this connector may carry. A submission naming another one is refused.

hooks.description: The `kind` an event may declare and the hook it fires. A kind absent from this map is refused.

inactive.description: Faces the connector declared that are not in force, with the reason. Never silent.

limits.description: What this connector may spend. Each class is budgeted separately so a flood in one cannot starve stop, which has a budget of its own.

submitParams.description: `mason/submit`: a person's words. Only a submission creates ordinary human conversation. `submissionId` is the connector's durable identity for the act; mason deduplicates on it forever.

capabilities.description: What this origin can render. Narrower than the hello declaration when one connector carries two surfaces of different ability.

approver.description: Whether the submitting actor claims approval authority. Mason decides: a claim the roster does not grant is dropped, never widened.

fireParams.description: `mason/fire`: an unsolicited service event. It may steer work; it never creates human conversation and implies no reader. `payload` is untrusted data and never becomes an instruction.

summary.description: One operator-readable line for the trace. Not an instruction and not what the model is told to do.

controlParams.description: `mason/control`: the closed vocabulary a connector may ask for beyond a fire. It never reads anything.

reply.description: One sentence for the person who asked, or why it was not acted on.

interactionAnswerParams.description: `mason/interaction.answer`: a correlated answer to one permission request. It is not ordinary chat, starts no turn, and applies once.

settled.description: Whether this answer settled the request. False for a late answer, an unauthenticated actor, or a request that was already settled.

stateSubscribeParams.description: `mason/state.subscribe`: what this socket mirrors. A scope the connector was not granted is refused, not narrowed silently.

since.description: The last sequence a client applied. Mason resumes after it, or sends a full snapshot when it cannot.

deliveryStartParams.description: `connector/delivery.start`: the first notification of a streaming reply. Same `deliveryId` as its deltas and its final, so a connector never treats one reply as two sends.

deliveryDeltaParams.description: `connector/delivery.delta`: more of the same reply. A connector that did not claim `streaming` never receives one.

deliveryFinalParams.description: `connector/delivery.final`: the reply, sent once as a request because its acknowledgement is what mason records. A redelivery carries the same `deliveryId` and the connector must answer `duplicate`.

deliveryAck.description: What the connector answers a delivery with. `uncertain` is the honest report of a vendor outcome that cannot be known: mason records it and does not retry, rather than duplicating a message.

external.description: What the medium answered, for the trace.

interactionRequestParams.description: `connector/interaction.request`: one paused tool call, put to an authorized person. Its answer comes back as `mason/interaction.answer`, not as this call's result.

answers.description: The answers this request accepts. v1 is `allow` and `deny`; there is no standing answer.

interactionAck.description: Whether the request reached a surface that can answer it. `delivered: false` leaves the approval visibly pending rather than silently denying it.

stateSnapshotParams.description: `connector/state.snapshot`: everything the connector mirrors, from a sequence it can trust. A projection frame is the whitelisted transcript and nothing else.

stateDeltaParams.description: `connector/state.delta`: one monotonic step. A gap in `seq` is a full resync, never a guess.

expiresAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. An expired content id is a refused download, not a missing one.

error.description: The `data` of a JSON-RPC error object. `code` is a stable string so a connector can act on it; the sentence is for the operator.

deliveryTarget.description: A proactive destination: the connector and the conversation it names. Absent means the submission's origin, which is the only default there is.

pingParams.description: `connector/ping` params. The connector sends it on an idle socket, every 20 s by the protocol's own number; mason answers with `pingResult` and nothing else.

pingResult.description: The answer to `connector/ping`: mason is there, and this is when it said so.
